name: Germany, StVO §§ 8, 9, 10 and 37 (right-hand traffic)
status: draft: rules taken from the text of the StVO (gesetze-im-internet.de, checked on 2026-10-30), not validated on any data. Confirm with a local traffic-law expert before using results.
notes: § 8(1): at crossings and T junctions (Kreuzungen und Einmündungen) the vehicle coming from the right has priority (rechts vor links), unless signs 205, 206, 301 or 306 regulate it, or the other comes from a field or forest track. The road that ends has no priority of its own (t_junction none).
§ 9(3), (4): a turning driver lets oncoming vehicles pass; a left turner lets an oncoming right turner pass (oncoming_left_yields). Two oncoming left turners turn in front of each other: no holder.

Signs 205 (give way) and 206 (stop) give priority to the cross road; the engine's two-way-stop rule covers 206. The StVO has no all-way stop. If every approach carries a stop sign, no sign gives anyone priority and § 8(1) is applied (first_arrival false). This is an interpretation, not in the text.

§ 9(3), (4) also apply on green: green_rules, used when both have a circular green. § 37(2) Grünpfeil (sign 720): a right turn on red only after stopping, without obstructing; the CAT code's red-light rule (the one on red yields) matches it.

§ 10: a vehicle entering the road from private ground, a lowered kerb or a field track yields to all others. The CAT code's driveway rule matches it. Field and forest tracks (§ 8(1) no. 2) are not distinguished on WOMD-style maps.
Not modelled: roundabouts (§ 8(1a)), priority that turns with the road (abknickende Vorfahrt, sign 306 with a supplementary sign), and police or signals that override signs (§ 37, § 36).

§ 37(2) no. 1: on red, stop before the junction. A right turn after stopping, from the right-hand lane only, is allowed only where a Grünpfeil sign is fixed beside the red light. The maps do not show the sign, so a right turn on red is reported as turn_on_red_needs_sign.

§ 26(1): at a Fußgängerüberweg (zebra crossing, sign 293) vehicles let pedestrians who are on it or recognisably want to use it cross; approach at moderate speed and wait if needed (crosswalk 'on_or_waiting'). WOMD maps do not tell zebra from signalised crossings: a crosswalk without a light is taken to be a zebra. § 26(3): no overtaking at crossings (not checked).

§ 9(3) sentence 3: a turning driver takes special care of pedestrians and waits if needed (turning_yields_to_pedestrians). § 9(3) sentence 1: a turning driver lets oncoming vehicles pass, and cyclists also when they ride in the same direction on or beside the road (turning_yields_to_cyclists).

§ 25(3): pedestrians cross the road taking care of the traffic, at junctions, lights or crossings where traffic requires it. A pedestrian crossing elsewhere has no priority, the driver keeps due care (§ 1(2); unsignalised_road 'care'). The StVO has no unmarked crosswalk.
§ 10: entering the road from private ground or over a lowered kerb, a driver must rule out endangering other road users (sidewalk_crossing 'yield').

§ 5(4): overtaking pedestrians, cyclists or e-scooter riders with a motor vehicle, the lateral distance is at least 1.5 m in town (innerorts) and 2 m outside; the screen takes a lane speed limit above 50 km/h as outside town (passing_m [urban, rural]).
